chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, the brother of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Five are awaited with them unless they alter: the drowned, the one struck by lightning, the one with intestinal ailments, the one crushed, and the one subjected to fumes.'

key_terms.يُنْتَظَرُ بِهِمْ: Awaited with them (their fate is suspended)

ai.seo_question: Who are the five people whose fate is awaited according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines five specific categories of individuals whose spiritual status is suspended (*muntazar*) pending their final state or actions, provided they do not change. These include the drowned, the lightning-struck, those suffering from severe abdominal ailments, the crushed, and those exposed to smoke, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) applied to those who die without clear evidence of faith or disbelief. This classification underscores the nuanced approach to *ghayb* (the unseen) in determining the fate of those whose deaths were sudden or ambiguous.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq a brother of Shihaab Bin Abd Rabbih who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Five would be awaited with them unless they alter – (the one who) drowned, and the onestruck by lightning, and the one suffering from intenstinal ailments, and the one crushed, and one subjected to fumes’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ’Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Khaliq, brother of Shihab ibn ‘Abd Rabbihi who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Burial is delayed, unless there is a change, because of five kinds of reasons for death: Death because of drowning, sudden shock, internal (illness pain), crushed and smoke (fumigation).”’
